title: La Romagna tra VII e III secolo a.C. Storia e archeologia di un'antica regione italiana
summary: Romagna is the region in the north of Italy that occupies the southeastern area of the Po Valley between the Apennines and the Adriatic Sea. Between the 7th and 3rd century BC, the area is occupied by Italic peoples that belong to an archaeological horizon that cannot be traced back to the contemporary Etruscans of the Po Valley. This book analyses the process of self-identification of the Italics in Romagna with an approach that examines not only archaeological, epigraphic and historical literary sources, but also settlement dynamics.
